category: usenet provider (German-language, volume, flat-rate and prepaid tariffs with a 7-day trial)

free_tier.stated: A free 7-day test access that needs only an email address: 'Testzugang, den du ohne Einschraenkungen eine Woche lang nutzen kannst'; the access closes automatically after 7 days. Its data allowance is not stated.
free_tier.notes: The trial runs for 7 days; the unit list has no 'days' term, so the nearest term is none with the period named here.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap is published; retrieval is by Usenet article over NNTP
per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: 7.807 days of retention on the home page ('derzeit 7.807 Tagen')

egress.terms: Volume tariffs of 12 to 240 GB a month, flat-rate tariffs of 1 to 25 MBit plus an Unlimited tariff, and prepaid volumes

interface_detail: NNTP with free SSL; the vendor ships its own client and search index
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: Three tariff types (volume, flat-rate, prepaid) with an entry price near EUR 5.

limits.value: 12 to 240 GB each month on the volume tariffs

limits_note: Volume tariffs from EUR 4.95 a month, flat-rate tariffs from EUR 4.95 a month, prepaid from EUR 4.99; the page's prices are listed with 'ab' (from).
binding_note: The cheapest tariffs are volume-bound (12 GB a month at the entry); the Unlimited flat-rate is a higher tier.

identity_cost.detail: The home page offers 'Jetzt kostenlos testen!' with an email-address field, and the trial page says the access details are sent to the email address. Whether a card or phone is asked for is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Backbone is not stated on the pages read.
confidence_note: Entry prices, the trial and retention are from the vendor pages read on 2026-11-03; the pages are in German.
